victim.name: Jessica Lloyd
victim.occupation: Belleville resident whose disappearance triggered the final urgent phase of the investigation.
victim.location: Jessica Lloyd residence area, Belleville, Ontario

truth.motive: Maintains composure early in the interview, but the case closes around his vehicle, movements, and the forensic trail.
truth.method: Distinct tire impressions near Jessica Lloyd's home narrowed investigators to a vehicle consistent with Russell Williams's SUV.
truth.hidden_clue: Distinct tire impressions near Jessica Lloyd's home narrowed investigators to a vehicle consistent with Russell Williams's SUV.

witnesses.name: Russell Williams
witnesses.profile: Air force colonel with access to vehicles, strict routines, and the kind of public credibility that initially shields him from suspicion.
witnesses.persona: Controlled, meticulous, status-conscious, and careful with every sentence; he sounds calm because he wants control, not because he feels safe.
witnesses.knows: He presents himself as fully cooperative and insists the investigation is confusing professionalism for guilt.
witnesses.hiding: His composure fractures whenever investigators close in on the vehicle evidence, his timeline, and the search around Jessica Lloyd.

witnesses.name: Graham Reid
witnesses.profile: Young local man with emotional history, enough proximity to Jessica's routines to matter, and the kind of personal friction detectives would check first.
witnesses.persona: Restless, defensive, and eager to distance himself from the case; he sounds more rattled than calculating.
witnesses.knows: He can account for most of the night but resents being treated as the obvious first-round suspect.
witnesses.hiding: He left out a late argument with Jessica because he knew it would make him sound volatile, even though it is not the real answer.
witnesses.portrait_prompt: Graham Reid, documentary portrait, realistic, editorial true crime style

witnesses.name: Colin Fraser
witnesses.profile: Tradesman familiar with back roads, late-night driving, and the kind of alibi gaps police naturally pull on in a disappearance case.
witnesses.persona: Blunt, proud, and irritated by police attention; he sounds rough but not strategically polished.
witnesses.knows: He knew the roads around Belleville and had a practical reason to be moving around after dark.
witnesses.hiding: He concealed an off-book job because he feared tax and licensing trouble, turning a bad decision into suspicious behaviour.
witnesses.portrait_prompt: Colin Fraser, documentary portrait, realistic, editorial true crime style

witnesses.name: Adam Doyle
witnesses.profile: Support-side military insider with enough access to know what should and should not appear in vehicle and movement records.
witnesses.persona: Careful, deferential, and anxious about exposing institutional embarrassment; he sounds like someone trying not to implicate himself in a scandal.
witnesses.knows: He can explain how vehicle access and paperwork worked around the base during the search window.
witnesses.hiding: He touched paperwork after the fact to avoid bringing military humiliation onto himself and his chain of command.
witnesses.portrait_prompt: Adam Doyle, documentary portrait, realistic, editorial true crime style

witnesses.name: Jim Smyth
witnesses.role: OPP detective sergeant leading the interview strategy in Ottawa.
witnesses.profile: Lead interviewer who understands that the confession only lands because the facts are already trapping the subject from every direction.
witnesses.persona: Steady, probing, patient, and strategic; he sounds calm because he wants the suspect to fill the silence.
witnesses.knows: He can explain how the tire evidence, routine-building, and interview pressure converged on the same person.
witnesses.hiding: He knows which moments in the interview mattered most, but he is careful not to turn the truth into theatre.
witnesses.portrait_prompt: Jim Smyth, documentary portrait, realistic, editorial true crime style

witnesses.name: Carol Lloyd
witnesses.role: Family-side witness composite grounded in Jessica Lloyd coverage and memorial reporting.
witnesses.profile: Family representative who keeps the victim at the center of the story and resists letting the investigation collapse into gossip or spectacle.
witnesses.persona: Grieving, direct, and emotionally controlled; she speaks with moral clarity rather than investigative certainty.
witnesses.knows: She can speak to Jessica's routines, what mattered in the early search, and how the family experienced the case pressure.
witnesses.hiding: She deliberately withholds some of the family's anger because she wants facts on the record before emotion takes over.
witnesses.portrait_prompt: Carol Lloyd, documentary portrait, realistic, editorial true crime style

witnesses.name: Erin McAllister
witnesses.role: Composite coworker and friend who can separate rumour from the small routine details Jessica actually shared.
witnesses.profile: Close enough to know changes in Jessica's mood and schedule, but not so close that every memory is warped by panic.
witnesses.persona: Observant, emotionally direct, and less guarded than the suspects; she sounds like someone trying to be useful, not impressive.
witnesses.knows: She noticed subtle changes in Jessica's routine and can distinguish what was real from what people only claimed after the fact.
witnesses.hiding: She initially kept back an awkward conversation because she did not want police to reduce Jessica to dating gossip.
witnesses.portrait_prompt: Erin McAllister, documentary portrait, realistic, editorial true crime style

clues: Plaster forensic cast of a boot impression taken at the farmhouse rear entrance — tread pattern matches size 10.5 Canadian Forces parade boots recovered from Williams's Tweed residence.
Isolated 1920s limestone farmhouse, Highway 37, Hastings County — victim's residence and primary scene. Remote location; multiple unforced entry points documented.
Dark mahogany wooden box with brass hasp lock, recovered under floorboards of Williams's Tweed property — contents include personal articles traced to multiple victims.
Canadian Forces dark-blue colonel's beret with CFB Trenton insignia found in Williams's effects — his command visibility had initially appeared to rule him out.
runtimeCase.scene_prompt: Investigative scene reconstruction of The Belleville Vanishing, grounded in documented evidence and timeline details.
runtimeCase.brief: On February 7, 2010, investigators questioned Colonel Russell Williams at Ottawa Police Service while the search for Jessica Lloyd was still active. Tire-track analysis, vehicle scrutiny, and inconsistencies in Williams's account had begun to collapse the image of a disciplined air-force commander into that of the prime suspect.
